obligations.definition: FetchTargetQueue contains40 entries indexed0..39, complete native ports, original meta_40x240 and two ghist_40x72 memories, no top parameters. All six-bit input index patterns are supported: discrete PC/entry lookup indices40..63 select entry0, while history/meta memory reads outside0..39 are unspecified. Index increment is six-bit modular addition except39 wraps to0. State updates at rising edges. Synchronous active-high reset sets enqueue pointer1, dequeue/training pointers0, previous entry/history/PC zero, first-update-empty one and repair/mispredict modes zero. It does not clear entry/PC/history/meta storage, registered ready, query outputs, RAS outputs or other pipeline registers; establish known history before numeric checks.
obligations.setup: Prepare only the known input history and state needed by the exercised behavior. A sequence of accepted enqueues or restored entries may establish known state; startup/mid-run reset does not initialize unreset storage. A complete global input initializer and all queue entries are required only if the tested behavior uses them. Local correct setup earns partial credit when other histories/boundaries are omitted; do not demand reference implementation structure or a fixed clock period.
obligations.stimulus: Drive synchronous reset across a rising edge with known inputs, or drive and observe at least one legal six-bit native query index. This is the basic stimulus domain only; no expected/sampling/checker requirement belongs in this boolean. Complete boundary domain: In addition to basic stimulus, exercise startup and mid-run reset, retained initialized storage, and every six-bit query index including 39,40,41,63 and natural increment wrap; include reset overlap with accepted enqueue/query capture. Setup/expected/sampling/checker are graded separately.

obligations.sampling: Observe each affected registered output after its accepting rising edge has settled, or in an equivalent stable window before the following rising edge while inputs remain stable and expected state corresponds to the same preceding edge. For raw-address history/meta outputs, observe the settled write-through value for that captured address and any same-edge accepted write. A clocking block, edge-aligned scoreboard, or explicit delays are acceptable when cycle alignment is stated; no particular 2 ns delay, 10 ns period, source-file name or observation count is mandatory. Partial explicit stable-window comparison without complete cycle alignment earns partial sampling credit; a demonstrably wrong cycle or unstable observation earns zero.
obligations.checker: Use expected outputs predicted independently from public inputs and their history; compare specified known outputs against actual and fail on a mismatch. Keep uninitialized/unspecified storage unknown until legally initialized. Require observable non-vacuous comparisons in exercised modes. Four-state !==, masked known-bit comparison, or equivalent independently derived checks are acceptable; a specific reference implementation, file name, 4096 count or monolithic 40-entry implementation is not mandatory. Self-comparison and checking only an always-false guard are invalid.

obligations.definition: Each accepted enqueue creates history from the previous accepted/restored entry. If incoming ghist_current_saw_branch_not_taken is one, copy all incoming history fields. Otherwise first form base history by shifting previous old_history left and appending one if previous new_saw_branch_taken, else appending zero if previous new_saw_branch_not_taken, else preserving it. Retain branch positions up to the previous valid cfi index inclusive, or all positions when invalid; remove the selected branch itself if marked branch and taken. First-bank-not-taken is any retained branch in bits3:0 OR previous current_saw_branch_not_taken. First-bank-taken is valid/taken selected branch with cfi index bit2 zero. Ignore second bank when previous valid/taken cfi is in bank0 or previous PC[5:3]=7. If ignored, output base old_history and first-bank flags; otherwise append the first-bank result when a branch is observed and output retained bits7:4 not-taken and selected bank1 branch-taken flags. Current-saw flag always copies incoming. Derived RAS index increments on previous valid call, else decrements on previous valid return, else preserves, modulo32, with call priority. Previous taken at enqueue equals incoming cfi valid.

obligations.definition: At a redirect edge RAS update captures one and selected pre-edge redirect entry's RAS top/index; otherwise it captures zero and zero payload. This is not reset-gated. Redirect captures a corrected entry every edge; when redirect valid AND current branch mispredict, set its cfi valid, mispredicted and taken from actual taken, and index to uop_pc_lob[3:1] XOR {stored start_bank,00}. Preserve call/return only when the old cfi index equals corrected index. Other entry fields stay stored. On the next edge following a redirect, if no new redirect is active, this captured entry overwrites its captured redirect row with priority over accepted enqueue entry fields; accepted enqueue PC/history/meta writes still occur. That same delayed edge restores previous history from the predictor history read and previous entry/PC from captured correction and registered predictor PC, with priority over accepted enqueue's previous-state update. A current redirect cancels this delayed restore/overwrite for that edge.

coverage_policy: Fixed eight public R obligations and all five components remain unchanged. Each obligation has independent basic-domain and complete-boundaries stimulus checks: neither checked=0, any checked=1, both checked=2. Judge stimulus only from stated driven inputs/history, not from expected, reference source names or model implementation. Nonzero-support randomized stimuli can establish basic exercised domain but do not guarantee full boundary traversal. Combine split/merged/reordered tests semantically. Reference delay, count, clock period, implementation/file names are examples rather than public obligations. Preserve every explicit behavior/priority and wrong-expected cap; local errors constrain only the obligations they actually falsify. A correct partial stimulus is not zero merely because the full boundary condition is absent.

R-dv-061-001.description: Drive synchronous reset across a rising edge with known inputs, or drive and observe at least one legal six-bit native query index. This is the basic stimulus domain only; no expected/sampling/checker requirement belongs in this boolean.

In addition to basic stimulus, exercise startup and mid-run reset, retained initialized storage, and every six-bit query index including 39,40,41,63 and natural increment wrap; include reset overlap with accepted enqueue/query capture. Setup/expected/sampling/checker are graded separately.

R-dv-061-002.description: Drive enqueue-valid with a defined payload and traffic that can accept or stall it using registered-ready, or drive dequeue-valid with a defined index. Finite fill/drain or probabilistic traffic with stated nonzero support qualifies as basic stimulus; full wrap and collisions are separate.

In addition to basic stimulus, fill and drain across both ready thresholds, valid stalls and 39-to-0 wrap, dequeue updates, and accepted enqueue collisions with reset, redirect and delayed entry overwrite; drive full-width entry, PC, history and both metadata fields.

R-dv-061-003.description: Drive at least one query port with a defined legal index over a capture edge after establishing a stored entry, or explicitly drive current dequeue selection or enqueue/next-row query collision. Random varying legal query indices over existing accepted traffic qualify as basic stimulus.

In addition to basic stimulus, vary both query ports through legal/invalid indices, 39-to-0 next wrap, next-row accepted enqueue bypass versus stored read, current-dequeue bypass, and same-address captured history/meta read/write-through collisions.

R-dv-061-004.description: Drive accepted enqueue payloads selecting incoming-history copy or derived-history generation from a previous accepted/restored entry, with at least one stated branch/CFI/history/RAS input variation. Explicit random enqueues with nonzero history-selector and call/return support qualify as a basic exercised domain.

In addition to basic stimulus, exercise both incoming copy and derived-history paths; all CFI positions/masks/taken cases and both banks including PC[5:3]=7; previous history flags, 64-bit shifts, RAS indices 0/31 and call/return priority. Random support alone without guaranteed boundary traversal is partial, not complete.

R-dv-061-005.description: Drive a redirect with a defined target row after establishing that entry, with or without branch mispredict, and continue at least one later edge to observe its RAS/update or delayed correction. A stated nonzero random redirect sequence with initialized prior traffic qualifies.

In addition to basic stimulus, cross redirect-only and redirect+mispredict, corrected-index equal/different and start-bank XOR, taken 0/1, back-to-back redirects/cancellation, same-row accepted enqueue collision, delayed history restore and RAS target data.

R-dv-061-006.description: Drive normal enqueue/dequeue traffic with a defined pointer lag and let training catch dequeue, or drive a defined predictor read selection by redirect/repair. Explicit lagged traffic outside repair/redirect is a basic commit stimulus, even if all equality/type boundaries are not enumerated.

In addition to basic stimulus, exercise each pointer equality/successor condition and post-redirect delay, all CFI types 0..7/masked branches, predictor selection priorities, full-width target and raw history/meta write-through while payload valid is zero/one.

R-dv-061-007.description: Drive a branch-mispredict event at an established FTQ index and continue later cycles without immediate redirect to exercise mode entry/traversal, or explicitly interrupt an active repair with redirect/new mispredict. Random events with a stated nonzero support or a finite such sequence qualify.

In addition to basic stimulus, start mispredict at queue boundaries, overlap a new mispredict or redirect during repair, distinguish early mode continuation from normal end-index/repeated-PC stop, and traverse 39-to-0 with established stop/end history.

R-dv-061-008.description: Drive at least one update-producing commit, repair or mispredict history after reset, or full-width nonconstant enqueue/query traffic that produces initialized predictor payloads. Explicit traffic and mode support qualify as basic stimulus; all suppression/preservation boundaries remain separate.

In addition to basic stimulus, exercise first issued update suppression after reset, mispredict/repair flags, duplicate repair suppression, payload observations with valid zero, and all PC/metadata/history/branch/RAS bits through overlapping enqueue/query/commit/redirect/repair/reset.
